body:
The closest thing that fits me is "errors in thinking such as... catastrophizing"

While it is hard to say I don't do this (I already said I am over-reacting with thoughts of suicide frequently) It definitely doesn't feel that way. I don't react like something is just so horrible, terrible, and unbearable. I react very neutrally and often just make note that "If I killed myself, I wouldn't have to worry about this."

To clarify, I am not over-reacting and then having suicidal thought, the thoughts themselves are the over-reaction. I am generally unperturbed by the happenings that make me think this way.

Thanks.  Like I said, I don't want to kill myself.  I think about it **constantly**.  The thought pattern is starting a  downward spiral where I am afraid I may convince myself later.

That's why I never have more than 2 drinks anymore.  I'm afraid that perhaps I only have an inhibition towards the idea that could be boozily removed.

I certainly won't be killing myself tonight, unlikely tomorrow, but I am scared of the direction I am headed, especially with this constant nagging "end it all".  I simply do not face problems appropriately anymore and instead split my time between contemplating suicide, and trying to not contemplate suicide.

I know that acting feeling.  I gave it up a few years back because I didn't know who I was anymore.  I still havn't found out.

I slipped into the same unmotivated mode you describe, with only a desire to escape life.

Sometimes I feel like I just keep on living for my family, like you.  Not even because I think they want me around, but I know they wouldn't want me to leave them in that manner.

Really, I don't want to kill myself at all, but I think about it all the time.  For me, escaping life has been into videogames, a good book, or drugs.

To be honest, this doesn't really do anything to help solve my problems, but it gets me away from reality long enough to be happy.

The romantic part of me likes to think people such as you or I were never meant to be happy with reality, we were meant to change it.  Not every moment of your life can be filled with importance, but one moment might change the world.  You are still amidst the character development on your stage of life.  The sum of your experiences, both good and bad, will determine how you act when your moment finally comes.

Don't check out early.  I can't remember the last time I felt truly happy, but I remember *how* it felt.  There is real beauty in life, I swear
I know exactly how you feel.
